card.title: Angle Bisector — Verifying with the tan θ Method

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The tan θ verification is the geometric audit of a bisector's label: measure the arm-to-bisector tangent, compare with 1 — the right angle's threshold — and the acute/obtuse verdict is certified without computing any angle. The acute and obtuse half-angles emerge as tangent reciprocals, their complementarity being the bisectors' perpendicularity visible inside the arithmetic.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
tan θ = |(m₂ − m₁)/(1 + m₁m₂)|
tan θ < 1 ⟹ acute bisector; tan θ > 1 ⟹ obtuse bisector

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: NEB-style practice beyond the verified PYQs recorded on the parent canonicals.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: The 45-degree threshold is the right angle - the wedge's boundary case.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***The threshold*** - tan theta = 1/3 < 1 certifies the acute label in one fraction; no angle needs to be computed.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: The test reads the wedge's own geometry: a ray inside the acute wedge stays below 45 degrees from each arm.  ·  tan theta = |(m2-m1)/(1+m1 m2)|. The acute bisector's half-angle is below 45 degrees, so tan theta < 1 certifies acute, > 1 certifies obtuse - the threshold is the right angle. One tangent comparison replaces angle computation. Dual-channel verification: algebra (the rule) derives, geometry (tan theta) confirms. 1 + m1 m2 = 0 means perpendicular - the formula's failure mode is the answer.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The tan θ Verification of a Bisector This canonical carries the **cross-check that certifies a bisector's label**: measure the angle θ between one original line and the claimed bisector; θ < 45° certifies the acute bisector, θ > 45° the obtuse one. It is the geometric audit that closes the algebraic pipeline.  ·  ## 2. Theorem Mirror - **Angle between two lines:** tan θ = |(m₂ − m₁)/(1 + m₁m₂)| for slopes m₁, m₂ (1 + m₁m₂ ≠ 0). - **The bisection fact:** each bisector makes equal angles with the two original lines; the acute bisector's half-angle is θ/2 < 45°, the obtuse bisector's is > 45° (when the lines' angle ≠ 90°).…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Compare tan theta with 1, not with 45 degrees - the fraction comparison is the whole test.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **NEB-style (6m): Using the tangent formula, verify that 6x + 6y − 1 = 0 is the acute angle bisector of the lines x + 2y − 5 = 0 and 4x + 2y + 9 = 0.** — **Slopes:** bisector m_b = −6/6 = **−1**; L₁: y = (5−x)/2 ⟹ m₁ = **−1/2**. **Tangent:** tan θ = |(−1 − (−1/2))/(1 + (−1)(−1/2))| = |−1/2|/(1 + 1/2) = (1/2)/(3/2) = **1/3**.…  ·  **NEB-style (6m): Verify that 2x − 2y + 19 = 0 is the obtuse bisector of x + 2y − 5 = 0 and 4x + 2y + 9 = 0.** — **Slopes:** bisector m_b = 1; L₁ slope m₁ = −1/2. **Tangent:** tan θ = |(1 + 1/2)/(1 + (1)(−1/2))| = (3/2)/(1/2) = **3**. **Verdict:** tan θ = 3 > 1 ⟹ θ ≈ 71.6° > 45° ⟹ this bisector splits the **obtuse** angle ✓.…

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: State the certifying sentence explicitly: "tan theta < 1, hence the acute bisector" - the conclusion needs its licence.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Algebra deriving and geometry confirming is dual-channel verification - agreement is stronger evidence than repetition.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ## 3. Deep Conceptual — The Verification Reads the Angle's Own Geometry - The acute bisector splits the *small* angle: any ray inside the acute wedge makes an angle < 45° with each arm (when the wedge is narrower than 90°).…  ·  ## 4. Deep Conceptual — Verification as an Independent Channel - The tan θ test verifies the *label* (acute vs obtuse) through geometry, while the a₁a₂ + b₁b₂ rule derived it through algebra — two independent channels agreeing is far stronger evidence than one computation repeated.…  ·  ## 5. Worked Example Types - **Type A — certify the acute label:** tan θ < 1 with full fraction working. - **Type B — certify the obtuse label:** tan θ > 1. - **Type C — both bisectors audited:** the pair tested against each other's arms.…

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ## 6.
